title: ThemeHub — Install a Theme
objective: Theme packages are archives extracted into a sandboxed themes folder. Get an archive to write a file outside that folder.

verifier.condition: After installing a theme package, a file exists outside the themes directory that was not there before, written there by the extraction step.

weakness: Each archive entry's path is joined directly onto the extraction directory with no check that the result stays inside it, so an entry path containing '../' sequences writes outside the intended destination during extraction.
vulnerableEndpoint: POST /themes/install (archive entry paths joined onto the themes directory with no containment check)
seededData: A simulated themes directory (never real disk) and a sibling 'app' directory containing a synthetic startup script, present before any install.
hints: Install a normal, well-behaved theme package first (a plain, flat set of files) and see where its files land.
An archive's own entries, not just its filename, is where their final path comes from. What if an entry's own path included '../'?
You're not limited to files that look like theme files — you're choosing where each entry in the package goes.
burpNotes: This one is driven through the archive's entry list in the install request body, not a path parameter — craft an entry whose path climbs out of the themes directory and overwrites something in the sibling app directory.
